[1] THE DENOMINATOR, which this row said must be established FIRST. READ FROM THE CODE, not inferred: provenance.coverage() divides MEASURED by `total`, and _pnl_provenance.block_for_rows sets total=len(rows) -- i.e. EVERY row in the population, so FABRICATED and UNVERIFIED rows are in the denominator and in neither published count. MEASURED 2026-09-22T12:36:53Z, GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/stats: paper pnlCoverage 0.2236, M=267, E=664. Population (dashboard.py::_pnl_provenance_for): status='closed' AND is_backtest=0 AND pnl IS NOT NULL AND account_class='paper' AND strategy_name!='orphan_adopt' AND reconcile_status!='superseded', n=1,194 -> M 267 (22.4%) / E 664 (55.6%) / F 128 (10.7%) / U 135 (11.3%). REAL: n=431 -> M 329 / E 20 / F 4 / U 78, cov 0.7633. So 'the paper book is 78% estimated' is FALSE and must not be requoted; it is 55.6% estimated with a further 22% carrying no usable anchor at all. INSTRUMENT VALIDATED: I pulled the whole live trades table (n=6,059) via /api/diag/journal and re-classified it with src.runtime.provenance.classify_pnl -- it reproduces both published figures to the digit (0.7633/329/20 and 0.2236/267/664), so every decomposition below rests on the endpoint's own classifier.

[2] THE ANSWER TO THE THREE-WAY QUESTION IS (1): THE FILLS ARE MEASURABLE AND WE NEVER WIRED THIS PATH TO THE READ. Not a venue limit. Positive control, same account and same 14 days: 48 non-pairs bybit_1 closes resolved to exit_price_source='exchange_fill' (MEASURED) off the demo venue's own fills. The gap is one order path. MEASURED over the full table: 365 pairs_* closes exist, ALL on bybit_1, and **0 of 365 have ever classified MEASURED**. 0/365 is a structural exclusion, not a flaky lookup.

[3] ROOT CAUSE, one line and verified end to end. The bot's PnL-resolution contract (stated in order_monitor._sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit's own docstring) is: CLOSE PATHS LEAVE `pnl` NULL AND THE SWEEPS FILL IT WITH BROKER TRUTH ON A LATER TICK. BOTH sweeps select on `AND pnl IS NULL` (_sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit, _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced). The M22 pairs executor -- an ISOLATED 2-leg order path that never goes through multi_account_execute or the monitor's close paths -- computed and WROTE `pnl` at close time, under a comment claiming 'broker-truth sweep may refine bybit later'. THAT COMMENT WAS FALSE: writing the number did not race the sweep, it removed the row from the sweep's scope permanently. Everything downstream was already built and correct and needed NO change: clients.account_closed_pnl_for_trade's DEMO branch resolves from the exchange-fills store (#8111); the broker sweep stamps exit_price_source from the record and explicitly declines to relabel a pairs_* exit_reason (its guard 2 NAMES this path -- the author anticipated these rows arriving, and they never did); ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer is HOURLY to serve the 6h _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS window, and I OBSERVED it active on the live VM at 12:37Z with last_trigger 12:21:11Z.

[4] THE FIX: stop writing pnl/pnl_percent at the pairs close site so the row enters the contract every other close path already follows. exit_price and the candle_at_close stamp still written -- both are true at that instant and the broker sweep overwrites them together if a fill lands; if none ever does the local fallback prices the row from that same value, i.e. TODAY's outcome. So the change can upgrade a row and can NEVER downgrade one. UPPER BOUND over the live population -- NOT a prediction, and labelled so nobody quotes it as one: IF every one of the 365 pairs rows resolved to a fill, paper pnlCoverage would be 0.5293 and bybit_1 0.5657. Some fraction will not match (exit_from_fills refuses on qty tolerance and on its open/close window, and it refuses rather than approximating), and I did not measure that fraction. The floor is today's 0.2236, because the change can only upgrade a row. Tests: tests/test_pairs_close_provenance.py -- the old assertion `pnl == 20.0` was PINNING the defect and is replaced, plus a real-sqlite positive+negative control that a priced row is EXCLUDED by the sweep predicate, plus a source-read guard that both sweeps still gate on `pnl IS NULL` so a future edit there cannot silently strand this. 128 passed / 0 failed across every test file importing pairs_executor; 100 passed across the db-integrity + invariant suites.

[!] WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: under the promotion ladder, Stage 1 (bybit_1 / alpaca_paper) exists to answer exactly one question -- `do the mechanics work, and does REALIZED COST match what the backtest assumed`. A book whose P&L is predominantly ESTIMATED cannot answer a question about REALIZED cost. So Gate 1's instrument may be reading its own reconstruction rather than the venue, and E3's whole point was that the backtests were fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount. If the paper book that is supposed to check that assumption is itself largely estimated, the check is weaker than anyone has stated. [!] WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, STATED SO NOBODY QUOTES A NUMBER I DID NOT VERIFY: the DENOMINATOR of pnlCoverage. 266/(266+661) = 0.287, which is NOT the 0.2235 the field reports, so coverage is computed over a larger population than measured+estimated -- there is at least a third bucket (plausibly UNVERIFIED per src/runtime/provenance.py, which the rules say is never folded into measured). Do not restate 'the paper book is 78% estimated' until that denominator is read from the code. FIRST TASK OF THIS ROW IS TO ESTABLISH IT. [!] THEN: find out WHY the paper legs' fills are not measured when the real book's are (broker fill records absent for paper accounts? a different write path? an ingest that never ran?), and say whether it is fixable or structural. If structural, the honest outcome is a stated limit on what Gate 1 can conclude -- which is worth more than a fix that is not available.
